summary: Unexpected bulk CSV onboarding resulted in external invite links and transient elevated tokens
description: A scheduled HR onboarding import (bulk CSV) appears to have produced invite emails with unhashed external invite tokens and triggered an automation that issued short-lived admin-scoped tokens for a subset of created accounts. The import was intended to provision internal contractor accounts, but many rows contained vendor email domains and a malformed role mapping that matched the 'oncall-admin' template. This ticket captures triage, containment, and next steps.
impact: ~42 accounts created in prod-us-east; 18 invites went to external vendor domains; 6 of those accounts had automation-created transient tokens with elevated scopes. No evidence so far of malicious use, but tokens were usable for ~12 minutes before rotation. Potential data-exposure risk for internal metadata accessible to those accounts during the window.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Upload HR CSV to /admin/onboard with role mapping file v2
2) Onboarding service validates rows and writes to user-provisioning queue
3) Provisioner applies role template matching by role_key field
4) Emailer sends invite using token generated by token-service
5) Automation listens for 'user.created' events and creates short-lived tokens when role template contains 'oncall-admin'

investigation_notes: Initial triage: import was run by HR automation (cron job) using CSV retrieved from S3 bucket s3://hr-onboard/2026-03-13.csv
CSV contained 12 rows with non-corporate domains (vendor/partner). HR expected contractors but mapping file mismatch replaced contractor template with oncall-admin template
Automation that issues tokens is supposed to filter out external domains via allowlist but allowlist check failed due to new email normalization change introduced 2026-02-28
No external API calls from suspicious IPs detected during token window (per egress logs), but we cannot rule out manual click from vendor recipient

Recommend password reset for any internal accounts created and disable invites pending allowlist fix.

2026-03-13 15:52 - Jorge Ramirez: Applied hotfix to onboarding-service to reintroduce strict domain allowlist check and changed default role mapping to 'contractor-limited' when role_key is ambiguous. Deployment PR references above. Monitoring for similar jobs for next 24h.
2026-03-14 09:10 - Legal (Elena Park): Please preserve all artifacts. We may need to notify affected vendors depending on risk assessment. Requesting timeline and exported logs by EOD.
resolution: Containment applied: rotated signing keys, revoked ephemeral tokens, blocked the scheduled import job, and patched onboarding-service to enforce allowlist + safe default role. Follow-up: full audit of provisioner behavior and HR process changes required. Pending legal review for external notification.
next_steps: 1) Complete full audit of user activity for affected user_ids and verify no data exfil occurred (SRE + Security)
2) HR to validate CSV sanitization and switch to SFTP with schema validation before import
3) Add regression tests around email normalization and allowlist check in onboarding-service
5) Legal to decide on external notifications by 2026-03-14 18:00
